key_insight: Aeneas turns production Rust cryptographic code into a pure Lean model, enabling scalable machine-checked proofs of safety and correctness without reasoning directly about low-level aliasing and liveness.
engineering_relevance: This shows that verified cryptographic software can remain performance-oriented and deployment-ready across x86-64 and ARM, while still meeting maintainability and portability demands.
method: Extract Rust code into Lean using Aeneas's ownership-aware translation.
Build Lean tactics and libraries to simplify proof automation over the extracted model.
Use AI agents to draft formal proofs and assist with standard/intrinsics formalization, with Lean kernel verification.
evidence_signal: The authors report a 237 KLOC Lean development verifying 16.7 KLOC of Rust code, including safety, panic-freedom, and functional correctness for post-quantum cipher suites on x86-64 and ARM.
watch_item: The hardest parts still require expert design and review, especially cryptographic standards and platform-specific intrinsics, so full automation is not yet achieved.
paper_title: Scaling Verification of Cryptographic Software with Aeneas, Rust, and Lean
